content.comment_body: Hello, Has anyone successfully connected a [product_name] (version [version_no]) to Blynk using MQTT? I tried, but I am unsure which details from Blynk should be entered into each field on the authorization page of the device. Blynk provides an authorization token for each device; which field should this token go into? There are five fields during the second step of MQTT registration on the [product_name]: • MQTT Broker URL: I am using 'Blynk.cloud' • Port: 1883 • MQTT client id: ?? • Username: ?? (Is this your Blynk username?) • Password: ?? (I tried putting the Blynk auth token here). Any help would be appreciated. Regards, [user_name]

Hello, I received information from the Blynk forum: • Broker URL: lon1.blynk.cloud (or your regional Blynk server URL) • Username: device (in lowercase) • MQTT client ID: you can choose, any non-empty string up to 64 UTF-8 characters • Port: 1883 • Password: Blynk auth token. I followed these instructions and the [product_name] appears to be attempting to connect, but I get a 'Failed to receive data from MQTT broker' message. Can anyone help with this?

Hello, I managed to connect to the Blynk MQTT broker and the device shows online on the Blynk platform. However, my variables are not being published to Blynk and I am unsure how to resolve this. Blynk support said they are not familiar with the hardware and suggested checking their documentation, but it doesn’t mention [product_name]. Has anyone managed to solve this?
Hello, Just an update: We resolved the issue by using Node-RED as a link between the Hive MQTT broker and Blynk. Now, all variables from the [product_name] are visible on our Blynk dashboard.
Hi, Could you explain how you set this up?

analysis.insight_summary: Users trying to connect a [product_name] (version [version_no]) to the Blynk cloud using MQTT initially struggled to assign the correct values, particularly for the authorization token. While some managed to get the device online in Blynk, variables were not displayed. Integration was successful by introducing Node-RED as a middle layer between the Hive MQTT broker and Blynk, allowing all variables to be visible in the dashboard.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to easily connect their [product_name] to Blynk via MQTT, correctly map credentials, and see device variables reliably on the Blynk dashboard.
